findings.original_claim: Quick Review says SEP approved at each milestone review.
findings.replacement_text: The SEP documents the program technical approach. Apply the designated approval authority and approve before major-phase requests for proposals; update for substantive changes and applicable reviews. \autocite{DoDI5000-88}
findings.source_basis: DoDI 5000.88 (2020-11-18), 3.4.a; official indexed PDF retrieved 2026-10-20; prior correct detailed paragraph preserved.

findings.original_claim: No explicit teaching of image-only requirements feedback loops, design maturation, or MBSE pillars.
findings.guide_location: 17G / Requirements Traceability Flow; Program-Unique Specifications; Digital Engineering Policy
findings.replacement_text: Requirements traceability works in both directions: every requirement maps to a function and every function to a hardware or software element; each function and element must also be justified by a valid requirement. Design information matures from system definition and system specifications, through preliminary design and item performance specifications, to detailed design and item detail, process, and material specifications. Model-based systems engineering uses related models throughout requirements, design, analysis, verification and validation; its three pillars are modeling languages, methods and tools. \autocite[pp. 21, 28, 32]{edo-3-5-1-systems-engineering-overview-2025}
findings.source_basis: Coursebook visual pages 21, 28, 32; learning objectives 7a/8 and explicit MBSE teaching.

findings.original_claim: System specification derived only from CDD KPPs.
findings.replacement_text: The system specification translates approved Service requirements (updated SRD/CDD and applicable performance attributes) into system-level technical requirements and verification criteria. \autocite{edo-3-3-3-jfrp-2026,edo-3-5-1-systems-engineering-overview-2025}
findings.source_basis: Existing JFRP update; 3.5.1 pp26/31 retains old CDD-only language; harmonize with current guide requirements crosswalk.

findings.original_claim: System types reproduce 11 older categories despite citing current MIL-STD-881F.
findings.replacement_text: MIL-STD-881F provides commodity structures in Appendices A--J and common elements in Appendix K. Select the applicable commodity and tailor its structure to the program; use the edition incorporated into the agreement. \autocite{MILSTD-881F}
findings.source_basis: ASSIST MIL-STD-881 record, active Revision F 2022-05-13; live record 2026-10-20 describes A--J and K. Avoid asserting old 11-category taxonomy as F.

findings.original_claim: Guide does not demonstrate WBS format or evolution shown on coursebook pages 13-14/20.
findings.replacement_text: Example: a sea-system WBS places the Sea System at Level 1, Ship at Level 2, and hull structure or propulsion plant at Level 3. Training, system test, data, support equipment and initial spares are enabling branches, not ship hardware. As design matures, the Government proposes the program structure, contractors develop and update their contract detail, and the Government approves the agreed structure and changes. The level numbers illustrate this example rather than a universal limit. \autocite[pp. 13--14,20]{edo-3-5-2-wbs-2025}
findings.source_basis: Coursebook visuals 13,14,20; TLO5 format and TLO3 lifecycle.

findings.original_claim: Configuration Management Strategy assigns allocated and product baselines to contractor without phase or change-class qualification.
findings.replacement_text: Tailor Government and contractor control in the SEP and configuration-management plan. The lead systems engineer maintains the functional, allocated and product baselines under the PM. At completion of system-level CDR, the PM assumes control of initial product-baseline Class I configuration changes from the contractor; contractor detail design and internal control remain subject to that approved allocation. \autocite{DoDI5000-88}

findings.original_claim: Three types of baseline changes includes deviations and waivers, suggesting these always revise the approved baseline.
findings.replacement_text: An engineering change revises approved configuration documentation. The coursebook distinguishes a deviation authorized before manufacture from a waiver accepting a nonconforming item during/after manufacture. These authorize a limited departure rather than automatically revising the baseline. Current configuration-management guidance groups such departures as requests for variance; use the terminology and authority specified in the contract and CM plan. \autocite{edo-3-5-3-cm-tech-reviews-2025,MIL-HDBK-61B-CH1-2025}
findings.source_basis: MIL-HDBK-61B Change 1 (2025-08-15), current official indexed PDF https://quicksearch.dla.mil/WMX/Default.aspx?token=5796547 table definition RFV explicitly says no revision of product definition information; verified 2026-10-20.

findings.original_claim: Image-only configuration-control workflow and review entrance/exit criteria insufficiently represented.
findings.guide_location: 17I / Configuration Control; Steps to Effective Design Reviews
findings.replacement_text: Route an engineering change proposal through the configuration manager/CCB secretariat to the configuration control board. Record the board directive and obtain contracting-officer action when contractual changes are required before contractor implementation. For a design review, select entrance and exit criteria, assign reviewer roles, record and classify discrepancies, assign action owners, and track closure and error trends. \autocite[pp. 11,31]{edo-3-5-3-cm-tech-reviews-2025}

Product support analysis defines and verifies the support package. MIL-HDBK-502B (18 April 2025) provides tailoring guidance; the handbook is not itself a contractual requirement. Specify required analyses and deliverables in the applicable agreement. \autocite{MIL-HDBK-502B-2025}
findings.source_basis: ASSIST active revision B official catalog, checked 2026-10-20.

findings.original_claim: Image-only Ao formula, metrics and incentive examples missing despite TLO4/15/16.
findings.guide_location: 17J / RAM Metrics; PBL Metrics and Contracting Strategy
findings.replacement_text: Operational availability is uptime divided by uptime plus downtime; count standby and operating time as uptime, and logistics, administrative, corrective-maintenance and preventive-maintenance time as downtime. Pair a readiness metric with an affordability measure and a defined period: mission-capable rate, mission completion/MTBF, cost per steaming hour, and customer wait time/MTTR. Financial incentives can reward measured outcomes; option or award-term opportunities can encourage investment when authorized. Open architecture and public-private depot partnerships are nonfinancial approaches that enable competition and efficient support. \autocite[pp.16,26--28]{edo-3-5-4-acquisition-logistics-2025}
findings.source_basis: Visual p16,27,28; text p26; avoid treating slide incentive categories as procurement authority.

findings.original_claim: 70-80 percent cost share stated as typical program estimate; supportability diagrams omit trade relationships.
findings.guide_location: 17J / Support Costs and Life-Cycle Cost; Product Support Analysis
findings.replacement_text: The coursebook uses 70--80 percent O\&S as an illustrative life-cycle cost share; use the actual program estimate for decisions. Early design choices commit future support costs before cash is spent. Support analysis iterates through design, maintenance planning and sustaining engineering, feeding a configuration-consistent support package. \autocite[pp.20,23,31--34]{edo-3-5-4-acquisition-logistics-2025}
findings.source_basis: Visual conceptual cost curves and support-analysis flows.

findings.original_claim: Materiel release implies every release requires every deficiency closed.
findings.replacement_text: The coursebook describes full materiel release as certification that identified materiel/logistics deficiencies are corrected and initial support resources are available, while also identifying conditional release as a fielding issue. Apply the governing Service release process and document unresolved conditions, risk acceptance and corrective actions; do not infer that delivery or IOC proves all deficiencies are closed. \autocite[pp.68--69]{edo-3-5-4-acquisition-logistics-2025}
findings.source_basis: Coursebook itself mentions conditional materiel release p68; no unverified Navy release authority added.
